english: Let $\alpha>0$ and let $S$ be the circle $(x-\alpha)^{2}+y^{2}=4$. If the minimum distance between $S$ and the parabola $y^{2}=12x$ is $40$, then the value of $\alpha$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $\alpha>0$ तथा $S$ वृत्त $(x-\alpha)^{2}+y^{2}=4$ है। यदि $S$ तथा परवलय $y^{2}=12x$ के बीच की न्यूनतम दूरी $40$ है, तो $\alpha$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Distance between $S$ and the parabola $=$ (least distance of the centre $(\alpha,0)$ from the parabola) $-2$, since the nearest point lies on the normal through the centre.

For $(x,y)$ on $y^{2}=12x$: $D^{2}=(x-\alpha)^{2}+12x$, $\dfrac{d}{dx}D^{2}=2(x-\alpha)+12=0\Rightarrow x=\alpha-6$ (needs $\alpha>6$; for $0<\alpha\le6$ the least distance is $\alpha\le6$, too small).
solution_full: For a circle with centre $C$ and radius $r$ lying in the region $y^{2}<12x$ and not meeting the parabola, the minimum distance to the parabola is (least distance of $C$ from the parabola) $-r$, attained along the normal to the parabola through $C$.
Least distance of $C(\alpha,0)$ from $y^{2}=12x$: for a point $(x,y)$ of the parabola, $D^{2}=(x-\alpha)^{2}+y^{2}=(x-\alpha)^{2}+12x$, $x\ge0$.
$\dfrac{d(D^{2})}{dx}=2(x-\alpha)+12$, which vanishes at $x=\alpha-6$; $\dfrac{d^{2}(D^{2})}{dx^{2}}=2>0$, so this is the minimum when $\alpha-6\ge0$.
If $0<\alpha\le6$, $D^{2}$ is increasing on $x\ge0$, the least distance is $D(0)=\alpha\le6$, and the circle-parabola distance is at most $4$, not $40$. So $\alpha>6$.
For $\alpha>6$: least $D^{2}=(-6)^{2}+12(\alpha-6)=12\alpha-36$, and the circle lies inside the parabola's region because $\sqrt{12\alpha-36}>2$.
(The condition $\alpha>0$ excludes the second configuration $\alpha=-42$, where the centre is outside the parabola and the nearest point is the vertex.)
originality_note: New: circle-parabola distance reduced to centre-parabola distance, with the case split alpha <= 6 (vertex nearest) versus alpha > 6 and a sign condition removing alpha = -42 (way 5). Closest known: shortest distance between y^2 = 4x and a circle on its axis. Different because: the distance is given and alpha is recovered, which forces the case analysis.
blueprint_concepts: Minimum distance of a point from a curve

concept_use.Minimum distance between two curves: Distance between the circle and the parabola equals centre distance minus the radius 2, set equal to 40.
concept_use.Minimum distance of a point from a curve: Least distance of (alpha,0) from y^2 = 12x by minimising (x-alpha)^2 + 12x, giving sqrt(12 alpha - 36).

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, curve and function introduced with its domain; conditions complete; one reading of each sentence; answer unique and equal to the plan (positive 3-digit integer); Hindi mirrors the English maths. Added the condition alpha > 0 after the web check showed alpha = -42 also fits. Changed: alpha > 0 in the stem.
key_step: Minimise (x - alpha)^2 + 12x at x = alpha - 6 and subtract the radius.
justification: Standard reduction of curve-circle distance to point-curve distance followed by a one-variable minimum; a routine L2 chain like the area/conic anchor 2024-P2-Q2, well below the L4 inscribed-circle anchor 2021-P2-Q7.
